test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-5) Official Paper (Held On: 15 June 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Who among the following inaugurated the Indian Army Memorial in the famous Italian town of Cassino in July 2021?
solution:
The correct answer is __**MM Naravane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indian Army Memorial**

 
 
• From **July 5 to July 8, 2021**, **General MM Naravane**, the Chief of Army Staff (COAS), traveled to **Italy and the United Kingdom (UK)**.
 
• The Army Chief inaugurated the **Indian Army Memorial in the well-known Italian village of Cassino** and will also receive training at the** Counter IED Center of Excellence for the Italian Army in Cecchingola, Rome**.
 
• According to the Ministry of Defence, he will **meet with his counterparts and top military officers** during his four-day tour to Italy and the UK, , with the** goal of expanding India's defence cooperation**.
 
• Over **5,000 Indian soldiers **who lost their lives battling the **Japanese and German forces during World War II (1939 to 1945) **are **remembered **by the **Indian Army Memorial **that was built in Cassino town.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In order to fight for **Italy's liberation between 1943 and 1945**, about 50,000 Indian soldiers were sent there.
 
• According to former **Italian Army Chief General Fabrizio Castagnetti**,** the fourth, eighth, and tenth Indian Infantry Divisions participated** in both the brutal fight to take **Mount Cassino** and the subsequent difficult operation **to breach the Gothic Line**.
 
• **Indian soldiers** who served in Italy during World War II **are buried in other cemeteries throughout the country, in addition to Cassino**.
 
• During the Second World War, the Indian soldiers assisted in the **liberation of several Italian cities**, including **Luca, Perugia, San Marino, Florence, Forli, Cesena, Ferrara, and Bologna**.
 
• **Six Indian soldiers** who were fighting alongside other allied forces in Italy's liberation had also been **awarded the renowned Victoria Cross**.
